title: domain-skill/v1 body
description: agent-knowledge-governance-json-spec.md §4.4 — akg is the format owner (§5.3). Body is spec v3, the four-cell shape: questions → rephrasing → needs → queries. Each arrow is an inference the LLM would otherwise have to make; a skill is the answer key someone filled in ahead of time. `needs` is first class and a query is only the means of filling one, so a skill can say what it must know — and, when `filledBy` is empty, that it cannot get it. `description` is still NOT a field: the renderer synthesizes it, now from `questions`, which double as the routing signal. Unknown keys are rejected at every level so a typo cannot silently drop a rule.

questions.description: The user utterances this skill answers — cell 1, and the routing signal: the synthesized description quotes them verbatim, so they are written the way people actually ask, not as titles. Several because one phrasing does not cover how the same question gets asked ("값 어디서 오는 거야?" / "물리야 가상이야?" are one question in two mouths). They must be the SAME question — a second question the skill also answers means the needs differ, which is a second skill. Order is the author's lever: the description reads them in order, and a long list dilutes the routing signal, so a handful is the practical ceiling.

items.description: Spliced into a single rendered line — no newline, no leading markdown block marker.

rephrasing.description: Cell 2 — the question restated in a form that can be answered: the distinctions and domain terms the answer turns on, made explicit. It adds no intent the asker did not have. (This absorbed the old `intro`: domain caveats belong in the restatement, and the execution framing is the renderer's fixed text.)

type.description: Input-widget signal for consumers (issue #49): datetime = date+time picker (value convention YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm), date = date-only picker (YYYY-MM-DD). Omitted = free text. The value stays a plain string either way — this hints the widget, not the wire contract. Machine field like steps[].binds/table: not rendered into SKILL.md.

needs.description: Cell 3 — what has to be known for the question to count as answered, and where each piece comes from. This is the answer's floor (the 반드시 포함 line is composed from it), which is the inversion the v3 shape exists for: the answer decides the queries, not the queries the answer.

what.description: What must be known, in the asker's words — spliced into a single rendered line.

when.description: Condition on another need that makes this one active, e.g. `sensor_kind = PHYSICAL`. An inactive need is neither required for completion nor a reason to run its queries — this is what replaced the 갈림형 branch. The referenced need must exist and the graph must stay acyclic (envelope.mjs semantic check).

filledBy.description: Where this need can be filled from — OR: any one of them filled satisfies it (user decision 2026-08-04; an AND is expressed by splitting the need, which also makes 무엇이 비었나 visible per column). An EMPTY array is meaningful and allowed: it declares that this skill has no way to get this, so 답불가 is stated in the spec instead of discovered at runtime.

column.description: The column of that query's result this need reads. Pinning the column rather than settling for rows > 0 is a decision: when several needs share one query, a NULL column is exactly what a row count cannot see.

queries.description: Cell 4 — the means of procurement. A CATALOG, not a flow: order carries no meaning (this was `steps` until issue #46) and the only dependency between two entries is a `binds` reference by id. Which ones run is derived, not authored — a query runs when at least one need that names it in `filledBy` is active.

kind.description: How this is procured. One value today; the field exists because this cell is 조달 수단, not 쿼리 — an Initializer index lookup or a constant catalog lands in the same slot later, and a need can then list it as an alternative beside the SQL.

table.description: This query's source table (issue #44). Optional, and singular — every query today is a single-table SELECT; a join is where a plural would be discussed. Two consumers need it: a narrative prompt heads each data block with the table name, and the column meanings under that heading are excerpted from the db-schema doc this names (doc id = lower(table), so owner prefix and case do not matter to the lookup). `anchorTable` cannot serve — it is one table for the whole skill. A skill-level table list is NOT authored: derive it from the union of these (two places to write drift apart). Agreement with the sql's FROM is the envelope.mjs semantic check, which schema keywords cannot see.

binds.description: Executor wiring — where each :bind variable in this sql comes from (issue #32). Optional: a spec without binds is still valid for prose consumers, but a deterministic executor needs it. Keys are the sql's bind variable names; coherence with the surrounding spec (the arg exists in inputs, the referenced query exists and is not this one, no cycle, exact :var coverage) is the envelope.mjs semantic check, which schema keywords cannot see.

items.description: Shape contract 「끌리는 오추론」 — 「그걸 금하는 데이터 사실」, both sides at least 6 chars, single line. A count-only gate let a restatement of the universal discipline pass as domain knowledge.

ask.description: Spliced into a single rendered line — no newline, no leading markdown block marker.
